links.outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on hallucinations in static tasks and dynamic dental workflows
links.effect: RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, but its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.
links.quote: While RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.

links.outcome: Gap between static knowledge-task performance and dynamic simulated clinical dialogue performance
links.effect: Models show high proficiency in static objective tasks, but performance drops in dynamic multi-turn clinical dialogues. The bottleneck is active information gathering and dynamic state tracking.
links.quote: Our analysis reveals that while models demonstrate high proficiency in static objective tasks, their performance precipitates in dynamic clinical dialogues, identifying that the primary bottleneck lies not in knowledge retention, but in the critical challenges of active information gathering and dynamic state tracking.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs in simulated dental clinical interactions and specifically tests the impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on hallucination mitigation and dynamic workflow performance.
